prize_parts.citation: for the development of general, ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B068 with Buchwald and Hartwig. Round 1 did not produce a scientific argument that alters the merits. The method is general, mechanistically understood, reproduced for about three decades and used daily in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis. The credit is the cleanest on the shortlist: two groups developed the catalytic, ligand-controlled version independently, so a two-name citation excludes no one with a comparable claim. The chair asked for the conceptual distinction from the 2010 prize. The 2010 prize honoured palladium-catalysed C-C bond formation through the transmetalation-based reactions of Heck, Negishi and Suzuki. C-N coupling is not that mechanism applied to a new partner. The amine has to bind to palladium, be deprotonated, and then undergo C-N reductive elimination. Reductive elimination to form a bond to a heteroatom was the step that long defeated catalyst design, and it needed new ligand classes (chelating bisphosphines, then bulky electron-rich biaryl and trialkyl phosphines and later carbenes) before it worked. The kinetic problems are different (beta-hydride elimination of the amido complex, catalyst inhibition by amines and heterocycles), and so is the chemistry it opened: aryl amines, anilines and N-heterocycles, which are present in a very large fraction of drug candidates. That is a new bond-construction capability reached through new mechanistic understanding, not a further example of a prized reaction. I accept that this is a judgement and not a proof, and that members who see a family extension are not being unreasonable.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection remains the 2010 prize. A committee that sees C-N coupling as a successor to a recognised class will rate it below a new mode of action. I also accept that B057 has far broader opening support (three first places and six top-three placements against two and three for B068), and that B068 is not a candidate that excites the committee as a whole. Kosugi's tin-amide coupling and Migita's work are a real priority point: the transformation was shown to be possible with stoichiometric toxic tin reagents and narrow scope, and what changed practice was the catalytic general method. For that reason the citation should say general and ligand-controlled, which I have written into it. I do not think Kosugi should be added, because a third name would credit the precedent and not the general method, and it would also make the credit less clean than it is now. Finally, my weighting of synthetic efficiency is a disciplinary lens and I have no basis to say that the committee should share it.

responses.point: The chair accepts B068 is cleaner on attribution and maturity, but says that after 2010 a second cross-coupling prize invites the objection that it adds a bond type to a recognised field, whereas induced-proximity pharmacology is a new mode of action. He asks whether I see C-N coupling as conceptually distinct.
responses.response: I do, and I have set out the mechanistic argument in my case for. The difference is not the bond type but the elementary step: the 2010 reactions turn on transmetalation and C-C reductive elimination, whereas C-N coupling required amido-palladium chemistry and C-N reductive elimination to be made to work, which needed different ligand design and a different mechanistic analysis. I accept the force of the novelty criterion. I would only point out that induced proximity is novel in mode of action but still carries unfinished attribution and no approved degrader. If the committee wants a prize whose scope and credit are not open after the vote, B068 meets that test and B057 currently does not. I do not ask Heiner to rank B068 above B057 on novelty. I ask that the choice be stated as novelty against settledness, not as B068 being a repeat.

responses.point: Brzezinski accepts the maturity and clean attribution of B068 but regards it as a close successor to the 2010 prize, with Kosugi adding a priority complication, whereas genetic code expansion changes what proteins can contain.
responses.response: I accept that B054 is a different capability and not a successor to anything in the prize record, and I value that it is the broadest common ground on the shortlist (all eight proposed the same Schultz, Chin, Wang set). Where I differ is on how much the 2010 prize should weigh. Peter's own argument that the committee should consider what a prize changes in practice applies to C-N coupling as much as to code expansion, because it changed which molecules chemists can routinely make. I also agree with him that B054 credit is not settled: Mehl and Yokoyama are left out by the cap, and the 2018, 2020 and 2024 biomolecular-tool prizes make a further chemical-biology tool prize look repetitive. That is why I keep B054 as my second alternative and not my preferred part. I would support it as the fallback if B057 does not reach five votes and B068 does not either.

responses.point: Chabes and the other B057 supporters hold that Crews, Deshaies and Handa span concept and mechanism, that mechanism and generality outweigh the absence of an approved drug, and that Aili, Aqvist and Sparr also treat induced proximity as one achievement.
responses.response: The scientific payoff of cereblon is real and I do not dispute that this trio is the most defensible one for B057. My point is that the cut is not yet agreed even among its supporters: Linke says his Crews, Deshaies, Handa split is not firm and would take Ciulli over Deshaies, and Brzezinski and Zou argue Ciulli. Excluding Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim is a loss of credit that a citation naming both PROTACs and glues cannot hide. I also take seriously Heiner's point that the committee has not traditionally required an approved drug. I do not make the missing approval my main argument. My reservation is that the Crews and Deshaies PROTAC contribution and the Handa glue mechanism were different discoveries made by different groups, and I would rather see them honoured with the credit sorted out than now with the credit contested. If the committee does decide to go to B057, I will vote for the Crews, Deshaies, Handa configuration as my first alternative.

responses.point: Zou agrees with the B068 case and asks that the citation spell out the catalytic, ligand-controlled, general method so that Kosugi's precedent is handled precisely.
responses.response: I agree and have changed the citation accordingly: it now reads general, ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling. I think she is right that this wording deals with Kosugi without adding him. I would not go further than this. A citation that names the precedent would invite the question of Migita and others, and the prize is better served by describing the method that changed practice. I also share her view that, if the clinical evidence is judged sufficient, B057 is a legitimate alternative, and between the two of us that makes B068 a two-vote position; I do not treat that count as a scientific argument, and I would not ask anyone to join it on those grounds.

uncertainties: Whether a majority will treat C-N coupling as conceptually distinct from the 2010 prize, which is the decisive question for B068 and is a judgement and not something the record can settle.
Whether the B057 credit can be resolved between Handa and Ciulli, and between the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands, before the vote; the B057 supporters themselves state that their cut is not firm.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader is a disqualifying fact for a prize, or an ordinary stage in a field whose mechanism is confirmed.
Whether B054 is the better fallback than B068 if B057 does not reach five votes, given the recent biomolecular-tool prizes and the exclusion of Mehl and Yokoyama.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to any shortlisted candidate: none is a Lund, KTH, Chalmers or Tartu colleague or collaborator, and none belongs to the Masamune school. No recusal is requested. I repeat my disclosure that, as the only synthetic organic chemist on the committee, I have a disciplinary preference for B068 and that this is a bias and not a conflict. I also note the chair's remark that Sparr and I are Lund colleagues, which does not bear on any candidate.
